title: Generalizable Graph Prompt Learning Framework with Model-level Prompt Injection and Two-Stage Prompt Tuning

problem.claim: Graph prompt learning seeks to improve graph models across downstream tasks, but existing approaches have limitations in prompt expressiveness, prior-knowledge induction, generalization, stability, and tuning transitions.

gap.claim: Existing methods lack a sufficiently expressive and unbiased way to encode graph information and provide stable, gradual prompt tuning that supports robust generalization.

contributions.claim: The paper introduces GGPL, a graph prompt learning framework combining model-level prompt injection with two-stage prompt tuning.
GGPL pre-trains on subgraph structures and attributes, uses SimGRACE for subgraph similarity prediction, and applies self-generated prompt embeddings to integrate invariant knowledge.
GGPL uses transition tuning followed by task-specific tuning with learnable prompt tokens.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experiments on six benchmark datasets to evaluate the model's effectiveness.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph prompt learning is presented as a way to improve graph models on varied downstream tasks.
Existing methods are described as biased or insufficiently expressive, weak at using prior knowledge and generalizing, and unstable under direct end-to-end prompt tuning.
GGPL addresses these limitations through model-level prompt injection and two-stage prompt tuning, supported by subgraph pre-training and similarity prediction.
The authors report evaluation on six benchmark datasets.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links prompt expressiveness and generalization to learned subgraph representations, invariant-knowledge injection, and staged tuning.

interpretation.claim: Prompt design may benefit from combining richer structural representations with a gradual adaptation process.

application.claim: For graph learning systems, consider pre-training prompts or representations on subgraph structure and separating transition tuning from task-specific tuning.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which components are necessary, how they compare individually, or whether the approach transfers beyond the reported benchmark setting.

unknowns: The six benchmark dataset names, task definitions, evaluation metrics, baselines, and numerical results are not provided.
The abstract does not specify the architecture, training procedure, hyperparameters, or component-level ablations.
The meaning and implementation of invariant knowledge, prompt embedding backbone, and self-prompt generation are not detailed.
